A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the scientific content, figures, and tables are unchanged.

before.justification: v3 reports original descriptive data analysis in Appendix D: Table 2 counts corpus reuse across surveyed benchmarks, including eight uses each for AudioSet and Common Voice. Model-performance comparisons elsewhere are attributed to prior studies.

after.justification: v4 retains the authors' corpus-reuse analysis in Appendix D and Table 2. These original descriptive data-analysis results qualify, although the paper reports no original model experiments.

M1.justification: The taxonomy in Section 2 is unchanged. Neither version introduces or revises a proposed algorithm, model architecture, training objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark and corpus sets used in the appendix analyses are identical. No training or evaluation dataset, task, population, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Appendix H and Table 4 retain the same literature-based comparisons between end-to-end LALMs and cascaded systems, including identical benchmark membership and qualifications. No original comparator evaluation is added.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the same corpus-counting scope and procedure. Benchmark settings and metrics described in Tables 5–6 and Appendix I are unchanged.

E4.justification: The corpus-overlap analysis, real/synthetic-data breakdown, and system-comparison analysis in Appendices D, E, and H are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: The descriptive statistics and literature summaries retain the same reporting practices. Neither version introduces original repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 2 still reports AudioSet=8, Common Voice=8, and LibriSpeech=7; Table 4 preserves the same relative-performance findings and exceptions.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The conceptual definitions and taxonomy are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an evaluation-focused LALM survey, a four-category taxonomy, and identification of challenges and future directions. The novelty claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning corpus reuse, contamination, model capabilities, and cascaded-system comparisons are identical. Section 7 and the Limitations section retain the same applicability boundaries and research gaps.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page GitHub link for the surveyed-paper collection, whereas v3 only promises its release. This supplies concrete resource-access information; implementation and experimental details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography content, and positioning relative to earlier surveys and benchmarks are unchanged. Reference text merely reflows after the expanded acknowledgment.

P1.justification: v4 updates author-affiliation markers, adds the NTU AI-CoRE affiliation, removes one contact email, and adds a funding acknowledgment. The scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author block is reformatted to accommodate the affiliation and collection link. The longer acknowledgment reflows references on pages 9–12. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–10 remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit collection link improves resource discoverability compared with v3's release promise, and the funding acknowledgment adds transparency. These are limited practical improvements; the scientific coverage, analyses, claims, and limitations are unchanged.
